title: Group chat rescue
subject: Islamic Studies
unit: Summer 1: Dealings with others and Important Lessons
source: Seeded from islamic-studies/y9 lesson 12 (Pupil PDF worksheet: group chat rescue)
intro: Lesson 12: Guarding the tongue: backbiting. To understand what backbiting (gheebah) is, why Allah compares it to something disgusting, and how to stop it

questions.q: Explain why backbiting is so serious. (4 marks, our own question)
questions.a: Allah likens it to eating a dead brother's flesh (49:12); it harms honour and trust; it is a sin of the tongue even when true (Muslim).
questions.model: Point 1: Allah's image. Develop: like eating your dead brother's flesh (49:12). Point 2: even true words count. Develop: the hadith defines gheebah as mentioning what he dislikes, even if true (Muslim).

questions.q: Carrying tales to cause trouble is ...

Group chat rescue in the portal response box: a class group chat starts mocking an absent pupil. Write three messages you could send to stop it kindly, and explain the evidence behind your choice. Start: 'Message 1: ...'
questions.a: Kind interventions (change the topic, defend the absent, remind of 49:12) with evidence
questions.model: Teacher writes message 1: 'Let's not talk about him when he's not here, it's not fair.'

questions.q: how does a person repent from gheebah?
questions.a: Stop, regret, resolve not to return, make du'a for the person and praise them where you spoke badly
Mentioning someone absent with what they dislike
options: Mentioning someone absent with what they dislike

questions.q: Back to our ponder: is it wrong if it is true?
